claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was a native of Side in Pamphylia who served as bishop of Beroea around 320 and was appointed Patriarch of Antioch from 324 to 330.
He was a leading opponent of Arianism at the Council of Nicaea in 325 and engaged in extensive polemic against Arians throughout his episcopate.
In 330 a synod at Antioch deposed him on accusations of Sabellianism and he was exiled to Trajanopolis in Thrace, where he died circa 337.
